overall: Independent re-check of the five reuse trials (Blender 5.2.2, one process at a time, -t 2). Everything numeric the helpers claimed reproduced: all 16 final seed-set scores and all five earlier-recipe scores match to three decimals when lib/texture_compare.py is re-run (also with each normal map remade from the stored height at the claimed strength: identical), the side variants (COMBINE height rule, shared slate layout, mud rule, wood height filters) reproduce, the finished colour of every seed set 1 re-bakes from the recipe bit for bit (0 differing dots), node counts re-counted by walking the built recipes match all five reports, and the half-tile test passes on all five surfaces (one tile and two tiles across: mean difference 1.9 to 5.8 of 255, big differences spread evenly, control 17 to 30). The snapshot checksums still match (7 of 7, no cache folder); every recipe imports the shared layers from the snapshot behind a guard that raises if a module comes from elsewhere; no shared layer is copied, shadowed or monkeypatched in any trial folder; new layers and borrowed code are declared. Same-kind score is meaningful: scoring each seed-set-1 tile against all six references, its own reference is highest every time (brick 0.654 vs next 0.317; wood 0.665 vs 0.352; metal 0.661 vs 0.425 slate; gravel 0.658 vs 0.485 mud; mud 0.497 vs 0.354 gravel, the thinnest margin). Reading by eye: brick, wood, metal yes; gravel yes at a glance (ragged up close); mud partly (no braided wheel ruts, mosaic earth, sparse stones). Versus each surface's earlier recipe: layered is ahead for wood (0.667 mean vs 0.606), metal (0.648 vs 0.579), mud (0.507 vs 0.391) and gravel (0.622 vs 0.380), but BEHIND for brick (0.615 mean, 0.654 best vs 0.725); the brick report says so honestly. Fitting verdict, plainly: no tracing, no per-element lists, no optimiser code in any trial (grep clean; hand tuning with the score in view only, tuned most on seed set 1). The one place reference MAP data enters a final tile is the height-from-colour rule: brick 2-number straight line fitted once to the reference height curve, metal a 12-point curve (24 numbers, hard-coded in metal_height_rule.py), gravel a 4-number colour-mix regression (defaults in gravel_height_rule.py); wood and mud final tiles do not use one (mud's optional box, wood's box were tried and not built in). I judge these as global few-number transfer curves measured once, which the project's own description_audit explicitly allows ('curves (control points) ... are fine'), so they stay within 'measure general character once' by the letter; but they are fitted to the very height quantity the score reads and are the biggest single score mover for brick (+0.116, 0.538 to 0.654) and metal (+0.083, 0.578 to 0.661), so those two headline scores are partly calibration and should be quoted together with the COMBINE-rule score. Also these constants sit in code, outside the settings.json that description_audit checks (all five settings files pass at 8 KB: 78 to 98 JSON numbers, no lists). What carried over: interface, COLOUR AND FADE, DAMAGE, MOSS, OUTLINE AND SHADOW, COMBINE ran unchanged by settings on all five; the LAYOUT had to be new for four of five (only wood used the shared LAYOUT, plus a 5-node turn); COMBINE's slate-only height rule is the one shared limit no setting can change (replaced after COMBINE for brick, metal, gravel; wood used tone_blend 0.8). Shared node share 83.5 / 86.9 / 77.5 / 54.8 / 56.2 percent (brick, wood, metal, mud, gravel); working-only share 78.6 / 86.9 / 77.5 / 43.2 / 56.2. Not re-run: the 'earlier layered brick 0.194', the metal-baseline stored scores for tiles other than seed_1, the Amount-0 independence tests, the GRAIN-mask half-tile (12.5 percent) claim, gravel's ladder, tiles_across 2 scoring, and anything about roughness/metallic/3D render.

It is global, two numbers, not per element, so it stays inside 'measure general character once', but it is the only place reference height-map data enters the tile and it is worth +0.116 overall (0.538 to 0.654, height group 0.299 to 0.597). Quote the 0.538 figure beside the 0.654.
The fitted constants live in height_rule.py (code defaults), not in settings.json, so the description_audit does not see them.

Seed set 1 was the one tuned on; seed sets 2 and 3 score 0.04 to 0.08 lower, so the 0.654 is flattering.

Not re-run: the 'first layered brick 0.194' (no picture of it kept).
